transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood CSM); Elena (Aurelia Platform), Rajiv (Aurelia Security), Priya (Aurelia SRE), Tom (Aurelia CTO)
Links shared: Pilot deck https://tinyurl.com/aurelia-redwood-pilot-deck, Benchmark sheet https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-aurelia, routing gist https://gist.github.com/aurelia-egress

Summary (auto-gen, brief): Weekly POC sync focusing on network fallback experiments and egress shaping. Discussed recent canary behavior, a surge during staging run, suggestions for kernel selection rollback, and next steps for SOC2/KMS info and VPC access.

Topics: network failover behavior, canary fallback thresholds, egress shaping, KMS/encryption, audit logs, runway for production pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we'll do a quick round robin on what changed since last week then get into the canary fallback experiments. Maya, quick high level?
[00:18] Maya: yeah hi, so we ran three staged bursts in staging with the new routing policy, two of them hit the canary threshold, um the fallback kicked in but there was a small spike in 95th peek latency, i think the KV cache warmup + egress jitter caused it, so we've got logs.
[00:36] Elena: to add, we saw some packet drops on the egress path from our hop in ashburn, i put the pcap in the gist, looks like MTU mismatch on one of the transit devices, not Redwood.
[00:52] Rajiv: just to be clear, security is OK with the fallback as long as audit logs are intact and no plaintext leaves our VPC, we need KMS integration notes and proof of CMEK usage.
[01:10] Samir: cool — i'll send the SOC2 appendix and the KMS integration guide after the call. quick Q — Priya, you ran the kernel rollback play earlier right? what were results?
[01:28] Priya: yeah, we did a controlled rollback on a single node, latency smoothed but token throughput dropped ~4%, i suspect a scheduling/quant path mismatch — we need the SE to look at kernel selection heuristics.
[01:46] Maya: that matches our telemetry, the new kernel uses a different quant path which trades throughput for tail latency. for the pilot i'd recommend a canary rule that keeps the older kernel for 50% of requests until KV warmup is stable.
[02:05] Tom: i just want to reiterate that our success criteria: sustained 95th < 120ms and no PII egress to non-encrypted storage. otherwise we will not greenlight dedicated.
[02:22] Samir: got it, that's our SLO. quick question on routing: are you comfortable letting Redwood provision a temporary route table in staging to test egress shaping?
[02:38] Elena: yes for staging only, but it must be auditable and reversible, we need the changes documented in the ticket.
[02:48] Jonah: noted, i'll take the audit ticket and link to the runbook.
[02:55] [interruption, background] someone: sorry mic —
[03:05] Maya: ok network details — the canary threshold was 300 concurrent sessions, fallback policy triggers at 75% CPU or 2 second queue latency, but when the egress path saw the MTU mismatch queues ballooned and fallback switched to the hosted variant, which had a slightly different model variant and kernel.
[03:28] Rajiv: question — when fallback hits hosted variant does payload ever traverse public egress? we need to ensure it stays inside the VPC peering or the private interconnect.
[03:45] Maya: good question, current policy prefers private interconnects; fallback to hosted uses our encrypted tunnel, but in edge cases the egress could use public overlay if interconnect drops. that's why we want the canary to prefer older kernel + local cache until tunnel is validated.
[04:02] Elena: please document the exact egress paths and when the overlay is allowed, security will need that for the review.
[04:12] Samir: will do. next up, metrics review — Maya, can you summarise the 95th/99th numbers?
[04:20] Maya: sure — baseline (no fallback) 95th=88ms, 99th=160ms; during the canary switch 95th spiked to 210ms for ~30s, 99th hit 470ms. after we reverted kernel it dropped back. These are from staging run v12.
[04:45] Priya: i captured the system queues, and there were bursts aligned with second-level GC on one pod. could be memory fragmentation from the new runtime.
[05:01] Tom: are there any safe knobs we can tweak immediately? i.e. throttle concurrency, bump timeout? we can't risk customer-facing SLOs.
[05:12] Maya: short term: reduce concurrent sessions threshold for canary to 200, increase KV cache TTL slightly to reduce misses, and set fallback hold window to 60s so it doesn't flip-flop.
[05:27] Elena: agree. also, can you include an option to force canary to only use private route if available?
[05:34] Samir: yep that's a configuration change we can push. we'll circulate the exact toggles.
[05:40] Rajiv: on the compliance side, what's the cadence for audit log retention in Redwood Privet — i mean Redwood Private — we need 1 year minimum and a searchable index.
[05:55] Jonah: Redwood's default is 90 days; enterprise add-on supports 1 year export to your S3. Samir can outline the export and search API.
[06:08] Samir: i'll include the retention options and the export runbook.
[06:14] Maya: technical deep dive note — kernel selection uses a heuristic combining sequence length distribution and avg latency; in your workload the seq lengths are spiky which biases toward the new kernel; we can add an override param per route.
[06:31] Priya: would an override break autoregulation? we don't want to be manual forever.
[06:36] Maya: the override is a soft preference; the runtime still evaluates CPU/queue thresholds. only use if the canary repeatedly hurts tail latency.
[06:46] Tom: ok, action plan?
[06:50] Samir: summarize — Maya will run 95th/99th table with canary preferring local kernel and private route, Priya will validate firewall/MTU settings, Elena will enable the VPC rule for staging, Samir sends SOC2/KMS docs, Jonah creates audit ticket.
[07:05] Elena: one more ask — we'd like a rehearsal of kernel rollback with a step-by-step checklist before we do it in prod. can we do that next Tuesday?
[07:15] Samir: yes, next Tue works for us, i'll send an invite once we agree time.
[07:21] Rajiv: i also want a quick note on encryption in transit: are we using TLS 1.3 on the interconnect?
[07:27] Maya: yes we default to TLS 1.3 but we'll confirm cipher suites.
[07:33] [silence a few seconds]
[07:40] Jonah: got it. any blockers?
[07:43] Priya: main blocker is temporary VPC permissions and firewall change scheduling — once that's done we can run the full egress shaping experiment.
[07:52] Tom: timeline: we want to decide on dedicated vs hosted pilot by end of March, so next 4 weekly syncs need clear telemetry and runbooks.
[07:59] Samir: noted. we'll prioritize the canary stability work.
[08:04] Maya: i'll also attach the kernel selector logs and heuristic snapshot to the benchmark sheet.
[08:11] Elena: thanks all.
[08:13] Samir: recap in writing: I'll send SOC2/KMS + export runbook; Maya will run the lat table and update spreadsheet; Elena enable staging VPC egress; Jonah create audit ticket; Priya confirm firewall/MTU. we'll reconvene next week same time.
[08:31] [meeting ends]
